Casey (People Ops): quick follow-up from the all-hands Q&A with a few clarifications: onboarding promo commitments, transfer handling, and how appeals work. dropping answers here so it's easy to find later. :spiral_notepad:
Ravi (Eng Manager): thanks. manager question: if we promise a 6-month promotion on an offer, is that locked in?
Casey (People Ops): it's a documented commitment but not an automatic salary increase. managers must record an "Onboarding Promotion Plan" in Offer Notes and submit a promotion packet at the promised time. final approval follows normal calibration and budget checks.
Evelyn (IC): can you paste the exact short wording we should put in offers? avoids messy language in calls.
Casey (People Ops): sure — copy this: "Onboarding Promotion Plan: target review at 6 months; success criteria attached; manager & peer reviewer named; promotion subject to calibration and budget approval."
Morgan (Recruiting): noted, we'll add that to the offer playbook and use verbatim.
payroll-bot: Reminder: salary changes go into effect on the first payroll after HR approval; retro-pay requires finance sign-off.
Ravi (Eng Manager): transfer case: if someone moves teams mid-cycle do they keep their original review date?
Casey (People Ops): yes by default. if scope changes materially, new manager can request a transfer recalibration; both managers + People Ops must approve.
Evelyn (IC): appeals timeline? was fuzzy during the session.
Casey (People Ops): appeals window is 14 calendar days from the calibration email. managers submit packets for their reports; ICs should discuss with manager first. we'll publish a tiny flowchart in the handbook update.
Casey (People Ops): adding one more — we'll publish the updated handbook snippet and templates by end of next week and run a 30-min manager office hour Q&A. drop any extra follow-ups here and i'll compile. :raised_hands:
